citation.authors: Reid S, Fan R, Venton L, Weidner A et al

cited_by.title: Breast cancer, triple-negative disease and screening

record.population: 687 Black women diagnosed with early-stage invasive breast cancer at age 50 or younger, Florida and Tennessee, 2005-2016
record.design: Observational cohort, genetic ancestry and disease-free survival, median follow-up 10 years
record.finding: Triple-negative disease and lymph node involvement were associated with shorter disease-free survival (hazard ratio 1.81 and 1.77). A higher percentage of West African genetic ancestry was associated with shorter survival in the hormone receptor-positive subgroup. Full-time employment was associated with better outcomes (hazard ratio 0.44).
record.note: US cohort; the abstract sentence on ancestry was cut off in my copy, so only the part I could read is used.
